input_schema.description: Timing of platelet count fall for TYPICAL-onset HIT (used only if type == 'Typical'). Pass any string if type == 'Rapid'.
input_schema.options: ['Fall begins <4 days after heparin exposure', 'Fall begins 4 days after heparin exposure', 'Fall begins 5-10 days after heparin exposure', 'Fall begins 11-14 days after heparin exposure', 'Fall begins >14 days after heparin exposure']

input_schema.name: timingrap
input_schema.description: Timing of platelet count fall for RAPID-onset HIT (used only if type == 'Rapid'). Pass any string if type == 'Typical'.
input_schema.options: ['Fall begins <48 hours after heparin re-exposure', 'Fall begins >48 hours after heparin re-exposure']

input_schema.name: nadir
input_schema.description: Nadir platelet count.

input_schema.name: thromty
input_schema.description: Thrombosis for TYPICAL-onset HIT (used only if type == 'Typical'). Pass any string if type == 'Rapid'.
input_schema.options: ['New venous thromboembolism (VTE) or arterial thromboembolism (ATE) ≥4 days after heparin exposure', 'Progression of pre-existing VTE or ATE while receiving heparin', 'None']

input_schema.name: thromrap
input_schema.description: Thrombosis for RAPID-onset HIT (used only if type == 'Rapid'). Pass any string if type == 'Typical'.
input_schema.options: ['New venous thromboembolism (VTE) or arterial thromboembolism (ATE) after heparin exposure', 'Progression of pre-existing VTE or ATE while receiving heparin', 'None']

input_schema.name: skin
input_schema.description: Skin necrosis at subcutaneous heparin injection sites.

input_schema.name: acute
input_schema.description: Acute systemic reaction after IV heparin bolus.

input_schema.name: bleed
input_schema.description: Presence of bleeding, petechiae or extensive bruising.

input_schema.name: pres
input_schema.description: Presence of chronic thrombocytopenic disorder.

input_schema.name: neW
input_schema.description: Newly initiated non-heparin medication known to cause thrombocytopenia.

input_schema.name: severe
input_schema.description: Severe infection.

input_schema.name: dic
input_schema.description: Severe DIC (fibrinogen <100 mg/dL and D-dimer >5 µg/mL).

input_schema.name: indwell
input_schema.description: Indwelling intra-arterial device (e.g. IABP, VAD, ECMO).

input_schema.name: cardio
input_schema.description: Cardiopulmonary bypass within previous 96 hours.

input_schema.name: other
input_schema.description: No other apparent cause for thrombocytopenia.

name: Step-by-Step Approach to Febrile Infants
description: The Step by Step Approach to Febrile Infants identifies low-risk febrile infants, perhaps better than the Rochester criteria.

input_schema.name: ill
input_schema.description: Ill-appearing based on the Pediatric Assessment Triangle (PAT)? PAT evaluates Appearance (tone, interactivity, consolability, gaze, cry), Work of Breathing (tachypnea, abnormal sounds, retractions, nasal flaring, positioning), and Circulation (pallor, mottling, cyanosis, bleeding). Any single abnormal finding = abnormal PAT.

input_schema.name: age
input_schema.description: Age ≤21 days? "Yes" if the infant is 21 days old or younger; "No" otherwise.

input_schema.name: leuk
input_schema.description: Leukocyturia present on urinalysis? "Yes" if urinalysis demonstrates leukocyturia; "No" otherwise.

input_schema.name: pct
input_schema.description: Serum procalcitonin ≥0.5 ng/mL? "Yes" if procalcitonin is at or above 0.5 ng/mL; "No" otherwise.

input_schema.name: crp
input_schema.description: Serum C-reactive protein ≥20 mg/L? "Yes" if CRP is at or above 20 mg/L; "No" otherwise. Only evaluated when leukocyturia is present and PCT <0.5 ng/mL.

name: Kocher Criteria for Septic Arthritis
description: The Kocher Criteria for Septic Arthritis distinguishes septic arthritis from transient synovitis in a child with an inflamed hip.

input_schema.name: weight_bearing_inability
input_schema.description: Child is non-weight-bearing on the affected hip.

input_schema.name: temperature
input_schema.description: Fever with temperature > 38.5°C (101.3°F).

input_schema.name: esr_40
input_schema.description: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) > 40 mm/hr.

input_schema.name: white_blood_cell_count
input_schema.description: White blood cell count > 12,000 cells/mm³.

name: Surgical Apgar Score (SAS) for Postoperative Risk
description: The Surgical Apgar Score (SAS) predicts postoperative risk of major complication, including death in patients undergoing major surgery.

input_schema.name: estimated_blood_loss
input_schema.description: Estimated intraoperative blood loss.

input_schema.name: lowest_mean_arterial_pressure
input_schema.description: Lowest mean arterial pressure recorded intraoperatively (mmHg).
input_schema.options: "<40 mmHg" (0 points), "40-54 mmHg" (1 point), "55-69 mmHg" (2 points), "≥70 mmHg" (3 points)

input_schema.name: lowest_heart_rate
input_schema.description: Lowest heart rate recorded intraoperatively (beats per minute).
input_schema.options: ">85 bpm" (0 points), "76-85 bpm" (1 point), "66-75 bpm" (2 points), "56-65 bpm" (3 points), "≤55 bpm" (4 points), "Pathologic bradyarrhythmia or asystole" (0 points)

name: Simplified Motor Score (SMS)
description: The Simplified Motor Score/Scale (SMS) simplifies motor assessment of patients with head trauma compared to the Glasgow Coma Score.

input_schema.name: patient_response
input_schema.description: Best motor response of the patient.
input_schema.options: Obeys commands, Localizes pain, Withdrawals to pain or worse

name: ATRIA Stroke Risk Score
description: The ATRIA Stroke Risk Score determines stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation.

input_schema.name: stroke
input_schema.description: History of stroke. Note: point values for the age component change depending on this field.

input_schema.name: age
input_schema.description: Patient age category.

input_schema.name: female
input_schema.description: Patient is female.

input_schema.name: diabetes
input_schema.description: History of diabetes mellitus.

input_schema.name: congestive_heart_failure
input_schema.description: History of congestive heart failure.

input_schema.name: hypertension
input_schema.description: History of hypertension.

input_schema.name: proteinuria
input_schema.description: Presence of proteinuria.

input_schema.name: egfr_esrd
input_schema.description: eGFR <45 mL/min/1.73m² or end-stage renal disease (eGFR calculated from MDRD equation).

name: Hamilton Anxiety Scale
description: The Hamilton Anxiety Scale rates level of anxiety based on clinical questions.

input_schema.name: mood
input_schema.description: Anxious mood — worries, anticipation of the worst, fearful anticipation, irritability.
input_schema.options: Not Present, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Very Severe

input_schema.name: tension
input_schema.description: Tension — feelings of tension, fatigability, startle response, moved to tears easily, trembling, restlessness, inability to relax.
input_schema.options: Not Present, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Very Severe

input_schema.name: fears
input_schema.description: Fears — of dark, strangers, being left alone, animals, traffic, crowds.
input_schema.options: Not Present, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Very Severe

input_schema.name: insomnia
input_schema.description: Insomnia — difficulty falling asleep, broken sleep, unsatisfying sleep, fatigue on waking, dreams, nightmares, night terrors.
input_schema.options: Not Present, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Very Severe

input_schema.name: intellectual
input_schema.description: Intellectual — difficulty in concentration, poor memory.
input_schema.options: Not Present, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Very Severe

input_schema.name: depressed_mood
input_schema.description: Depressed mood — loss of interest, lack of pleasure in hobbies, depression, early waking, diurnal swing.
input_schema.options: Not Present, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Very Severe

input_schema.name: somatic_muscular
input_schema.description: Somatic (muscular) — pains and aches, twitching, stiffness, myoclonic jerks, grinding of teeth, unsteady voice, increased muscular tone.
input_schema.options: Not Present, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Very Severe

input_schema.name: somatic_sensory
input_schema.description: Somatic (sensory) — tinnitus, blurring of vision, hot and cold flushes, feelings of weakness, pricking sensation.
input_schema.options: Not Present, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Very Severe

input_schema.name: cardiovascular
input_schema.description: Cardiovascular symptoms — tachycardia, palpitations, chest pain, throbbing of vessels, fainting feelings, missing beat.
input_schema.options: Not Present, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Very Severe

input_schema.name: respiratory
input_schema.description: Respiratory symptoms — pressure or constriction in chest, choking feelings, sighing, dyspnea.
input_schema.options: Not Present, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Very Severe

input_schema.name: gastrointestinal
input_schema.description: Gastrointestinal symptoms — difficulty swallowing, abdominal pain, burning sensations, nausea, vomiting, looseness of bowels, constipation.
input_schema.options: Not Present, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Very Severe

input_schema.name: genitourinary
input_schema.description: Genitourinary symptoms — frequency/urgency of micturition, amenorrhea, menorrhagia, frigidity, premature ejaculation, loss of libido, impotence.
input_schema.options: Not Present, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Very Severe

input_schema.name: autonomic
input_schema.description: Autonomic symptoms — dry mouth, flushing, pallor, sweating, giddiness, tension headache, raising of hair.
input_schema.options: Not Present, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Very Severe

input_schema.name: behavior
input_schema.description: Behavior at interview — fidgeting, restlessness/pacing, hand tremor, furrowed brow, strained face, rapid respiration, facial pallor, swallowing.
input_schema.options: Not Present, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Very Severe

name: Major Depression Index (MDI)
description: Screens for depression based on clinically significant questions.

input_schema.name: sad
input_schema.description: Q1 – Felt low in spirits or sad? Range: 0–5.
input_schema.options: 0 = At no time, 1 = Some of the time, 2 = Slightly less than half of the time, 3 = Slightly more than half of the time, 4 = Most of the time, 5 = All the time

input_schema.name: lost_interest
input_schema.description: Q2 – Lost interest in daily activities? Range: 0–5.

input_schema.name: lacking_energy
input_schema.description: Q3 – Felt lacking in energy and strength? Range: 0–5.

input_schema.name: self_confident
input_schema.description: Q4 – Felt less self-confident? Range: 0–5.

input_schema.name: guilt
input_schema.description: Q5 – Had a bad conscience or feelings of guilt? Range: 0–5.

input_schema.name: life
input_schema.description: Q6 – Felt that life wasn't worth living? Range: 0–5.

input_schema.name: concentration
input_schema.description: Q7 – Had difficulty concentrating? Range: 0–5.

input_schema.name: restless
input_schema.description: Q8a – Felt very restless? Range: 0–5. Combined with Q8b (subdued); the higher score is used for Q8.

input_schema.name: subdued
input_schema.description: Q8b – Felt subdued or slowed down? Range: 0–5. Combined with Q8a (restless); the higher score is used for Q8.

input_schema.name: sleeping
input_schema.description: Q9 – Had trouble sleeping at night? Range: 0–5.

input_schema.name: reduced_appetite
input_schema.description: Q10a – Suffered from reduced appetite? Range: 0–5. Combined with Q10b (increased_appetite); the higher score is used for Q10.

input_schema.name: increased_appetite
input_schema.description: Q10b – Suffered from increased appetite? Range: 0–5. Combined with Q10a (reduced_appetite); the higher score is used for Q10.

name: Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology (QIDS)
description: The Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology (QIDS) rates depression symptoms via self-assessment, also known as QIDS-SR-16.

input_schema.name: onset_insomnia
input_schema.description: Item 1 — Sleep onset insomnia (0-3).
input_schema.options: 0 = Never takes longer than 30 minutes to fall asleep; 1 = Takes ≥30 min to fall asleep, <half the time; 2 = Takes ≥30 min to fall asleep, >half the time; 3 = Takes >60 min to fall asleep, >half the time

input_schema.name: mid_insomnia
input_schema.description: Item 2 — Mid-nocturnal insomnia (0-3).
input_schema.options: 0 = Does not wake up at night; 1 = Restless, light sleep with few awakenings; 2 = Wakes up at least once a night but goes back to sleep easily; 3 = Awakens >once a night and stays awake ≥20 min, >half the time

input_schema.name: early_insomnia
input_schema.description: Item 3 — Early morning insomnia (0-3).
input_schema.options: 0 = <half the time, awakens no more than 30 min before necessary; 1 = >half the time, awakens >30 min before need be; 2 = Awakens ≥1 hour before need be, >half the time; 3 = Awakens ≥2 hours before need be, >half the time

input_schema.name: hypersomnia
input_schema.description: Item 4 — Hypersomnia (0-3).
input_schema.options: 0 = Sleeps no longer than 7–8 hours/night, without naps; 1 = Sleeps no longer than 10 hours in 24h (including naps); 2 = Sleeps no longer than 12 hours in 24h (including naps); 3 = Sleeps longer than 12 hours in 24h (including naps)

input_schema.name: mood
input_schema.description: Item 5 — Mood (sad) (0-3).
input_schema.options: 0 = Does not feel sad; 1 = Feels sad <half the time; 2 = Feels sad >half the time; 3 = Feels intensely sad virtually all the time

input_schema.name: appetite_decrease
input_schema.description: Item 6 — Appetite (decreased) (0-3).
input_schema.options: 0 = No change from usual appetite; 1 = Eats somewhat less often and/or lesser amounts than usual; 2 = Eats much less than usual and only with personal effort; 3 = Eats rarely within a 24-hour period, only with extreme effort or persuasion

input_schema.name: appetite_increase
input_schema.description: Item 7 — Appetite (increased) (0-3).
input_schema.options: 0 = No change from usual appetite; 1 = More frequently feels a need to eat than usual; 2 = Regularly eats more often and/or greater amounts than usual; 3 = Feels driven to overeat at and between meals

input_schema.name: weight_decrease
input_schema.description: Item 8 — Weight decrease within the last two weeks (0-3).
input_schema.options: 0 = Has experienced no weight change; 1 = Feels as if some slight weight loss occurred; 2 = Has lost 2 pounds or more; 3 = Has lost 5 pounds or more

input_schema.name: weight_increase
input_schema.description: Item 9 — Weight increase within the last two weeks (0-3).
input_schema.options: 0 = Has experienced no weight change; 1 = Feels as if some slight weight gain has occurred; 2 = Has gained 2 pounds or more; 3 = Has gained 5 pounds or more

input_schema.name: concentration
input_schema.description: Item 10 — Concentration/decision making (0-3).
input_schema.options: 0 = No change in usual capacity to concentrate and decide; 1 = Occasionally feels indecisive or notes that attention often wanders; 2 = Most of the time struggles to focus attention or make decisions; 3 = Cannot concentrate well enough to read or cannot make even minor decisions

input_schema.name: outlook
input_schema.description: Item 11 — Outlook (self-view) (0-3).
input_schema.options: 0 = Sees self as equally worthwhile and deserving as others; 1 = Is more self-blaming than usual; 2 = Largely believes that he/she causes problems for others; 3 = Constantly thinks about major character defects or personal shortcomings

input_schema.name: suicidal_ideation
input_schema.description: Item 12 — Suicidal ideation (0-3).
input_schema.options: 0 = Does not think of suicide or death; 1 = Feels that life is empty or wonders if it is worth living; 2 = Thinks of suicide or death several times a week for several minutes; 3 = Thinks of suicide or death several times a day in some detail, or has made specific plans, or has attempted suicide

input_schema.name: involvement
input_schema.description: Item 13 — Involvement (general interest) (0-3).
input_schema.options: 0 = No change from usual level of interest; 1 = Reports or shows reduced interest, but still enjoys some activities; 2 = Only occasionally shows interest or derives pleasure from usual activities; 3 = Has virtually no interest in formerly pleasurable activities

input_schema.name: energy_fatiguability
input_schema.description: Item 14 — Energy/fatiguability (0-3).
input_schema.options: 0 = No change in usual energy level; 1 = Gets tired more easily than usual; 2 = Makes a great effort to start or finish usual daily activities (e.g., shopping, homework, cooking, going to work); 3 = Cannot carry out most of usual daily activities due to lack of energy

input_schema.name: psychomotor_slowing
input_schema.description: Item 15 — Psychomotor slowing (0-3).
input_schema.options: 0 = Normal speech and thought; no slowing; 1 = Feels slowed down; speech is slightly slower; 2 = Speech is noticeably slow; pauses frequently; 3 = Extreme slowing; speech is monosyllabic; cannot make decisions

input_schema.name: psychomotor_agitation
input_schema.description: Item 16 — Psychomotor agitation (0-3).
input_schema.options: 0 = No change in usual level of activity; 1 = Feels restless; often changes position; plays with hands or hair; 2 = Cannot sit still; paces frequently; 3 = Constantly paces or wrings hands; cannot remain seated for more than a few minutes

name: Vancouver Chest Pain Rule
description: The Vancouver Chest Pain Rule identifies chest pain patients who are at low risk for adverse event and are safe for early discharge.

input_schema.name: abnormal_ecg
input_schema.description: Abnormal initial EKG (ST elevation, ST depression >0.5 mm, Q waves, LVH, paced rhythm, or LBBB).

input_schema.name: troponin
input_schema.description: Positive troponin at 2 hours.

input_schema.name: acs_nitrate_use
input_schema.description: Prior ACS or nitrate use.

input_schema.name: palpation
input_schema.description: Does palpation reproduce the chest pain?

input_schema.name: age_50
input_schema.description: Is the patient age 50 or above?

input_schema.name: pain_radiate
input_schema.description: Does pain radiate to neck, jaw, or left arm?

name: ADAPT Protocol for Cardiac Event Risk
description: The ADAPT Protocol for Cardiac Event Risk uses a 2-hour accelerated diagnostic protocol to assess patients with chest pain for 30 day risk of cardiac event.

input_schema.name: abnormal_troponin
input_schema.description: Whether cTnI at 0h or 2h is above institutional cutoff.

input_schema.name: abnormal_ekg
input_schema.description: Whether ischemic EKG changes are present (ST-segment depression ≥ 0.05 mV in ≥ 2 contiguous leads, T-wave inversion ≥ 0.1 mV, or Q waves ≥ 30 ms wide and ≥ 0.1 mV deep in ≥ 2 contiguous leads).

input_schema.name: age_65
input_schema.description: Whether patient age is ≥ 65 years.

input_schema.name: cad_risk_factors
input_schema.description: Whether patient has ≥ 3 CAD risk factors (hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, diabetes, family history of CAD, or current smoker).

input_schema.name: known_cad
input_schema.description: Whether patient has known CAD defined as prior coronary stenosis ≥ 50%.

input_schema.name: aspirin_use
input_schema.description: Whether patient used aspirin in the past 7 days.

input_schema.name: angina
input_schema.description: Whether patient has severe angina (≥ 2 anginal episodes in 24 hours or persisting ischemic discomfort).

name: Emergency Department Assessment of Chest Pain Score (EDACS)
description: The Emergency Department Assessment of Chest Pain Score (EDACS) identifies chest pain patients with low risk of major adverse cardiac event who could be discharged early from the ED.

input_schema.name: age
input_schema.description: Patient age in completed years (18–100). Age bands determine base points.

input_schema.name: sex
input_schema.description: Patient biological sex.

input_schema.name: artery_disease_risk_factors
input_schema.description: Known coronary artery disease or ≥3 cardiac risk factors (for age 18–50).

input_schema.name: diaphoresis
input_schema.description: Presence of diaphoresis during presentation.

input_schema.name: radiates
input_schema.description: Pain radiates to arm, shoulder, neck, or jaw.

input_schema.name: pain_inspiration
input_schema.description: Pain occurred or worsened with inspiration.

input_schema.name: pain_palpation
input_schema.description: Pain is reproduced by palpation.

name: APACHE II Score
description: The Apache II Score estimates ICU mortality based on a number of laboratory values and patient signs taking both acute and chronic disease into account.

input_schema.name: organ_insufficiency
input_schema.description: History of severe organ failure or immunocompromise; includes Heart Failure Class IV, cirrhosis, chronic lung disease, or dialysis-dependent renal failure.

input_schema.name: surgery
input_schema.description: Type of surgery or admission type; used together with organ_insufficiency to assign chronic health points.

input_schema.name: age
input_schema.description: Patient age in years.

input_schema.name: temperature
input_schema.description: Core body temperature in degrees Celsius (°C); use the worst value in the first 24 hours of ICU admission.

input_schema.name: mean_arterial_pressure
input_schema.description: Mean arterial pressure in mmHg.

input_schema.name: ph
input_schema.description: Arterial blood pH.

input_schema.name: heart_rate
input_schema.description: Heart rate (pulse) in beats per minute.

input_schema.name: respiratory_rate
input_schema.description: Respiratory rate in breaths per minute.

input_schema.name: sodium
input_schema.description: Serum sodium in mmol/L (equivalent to mEq/L).

input_schema.name: potassium
input_schema.description: Serum potassium in mmol/L (equivalent to mEq/L).

input_schema.name: creatinine
input_schema.description: Serum creatinine in µmol/L; internally converted to mg/dL for scoring (1 mg/dL = 88.4 µmol/L).

input_schema.name: acute_renal_failure
input_schema.description: Whether patient has acute renal failure; if "Yes", creatinine score points are doubled.

input_schema.name: hematocrit
input_schema.description: Hematocrit in percent (%).

input_schema.name: white_blood_cell_count
input_schema.description: White blood cell count in × 10⁹ cells/L (equivalent to × 10³ cells/µL).

input_schema.name: glasgow_coma_scale
input_schema.description: Glasgow Coma Scale total score in points; APACHE II contribution = 15 − GCS.

input_schema.name: fio2
input_schema.description: Fraction of inspired oxygen category; determines whether PaO₂ or A-a gradient is used for oxygenation scoring.

input_schema.name: pao2
input_schema.description: PaO₂ category in mmHg; used only when fio2 is "<50% (or non-intubated)".

input_schema.name: aa_grad
input_schema.description: Alveolar-arterial oxygen gradient category; used only when fio2 is "≥50%".

name: Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU (CAM-ICU)
description: The Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU (CAM-ICU) monitors delirium in ICU patients.

input_schema.name: rass_3
input_schema.description: RASS ≥ −3 (sufficient level of consciousness to assess). 'Yes' = RASS is −3, −2, −1, 0, +1, +2, or +3 → proceed with assessment. 'No' = RASS is −4 or −5 (unarousable/deeply sedated) → cannot assess.

input_schema.name: baseline_status
input_schema.description: Patient's current mental status is different from pre-hospital / pre-illness neurologic baseline. 'Yes' = different from baseline (Feature 1 criterion). 'No' = no change from baseline.

input_schema.name: mental_status
input_schema.description: Patient's level of consciousness or sedation has fluctuated over the past 24 hours (e.g., variable RASS scores). 'Yes' = fluctuation present (Feature 1 criterion). 'No' = no fluctuation.

input_schema.name: attention_test
input_schema.description: Standardised Letters Attention Test resulted in more than 2 errors (Feature 2 — Inattention). 'Yes' = > 2 errors → inattention present. 'No' = ≤ 2 errors → inattention absent.

input_schema.name: rass_score
input_schema.description: Current RASS score is anything other than 0 (Feature 3 — Altered Level of Consciousness). 'Yes' = RASS ≠ 0 → altered LOC present. 'No' = RASS = 0 → alert and calm, no altered LOC.

input_schema.name: error_questions
input_schema.description: Combined number of errors on the standardised yes/no questions AND commands exceeds 1 (Feature 4 — Disorganised Thinking). 'Yes' = > 1 combined error → disorganised thinking present. 'No' = ≤ 1 combined error → organised thinking.

name: Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS)
description: The Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS) ranks agitation and possibility for sedation.

input_schema.name: patient_description
input_schema.description: Clinical description of patient's level of alertness or agitation.
input_schema.options: Combative, Very agitated, Agitated, Restless, Alert and calm, Drowsy, Light sedation, Moderate sedation, Deep sedation, Unarousable sedation

name: National Early Warning Score (NEWS)
description: The National Early Warning Score (NEWS) determines the degree of illness of a patient using six physiological findings and one observation.

input_schema.name: respiratory_rate
input_schema.description: Respiratory rate in breaths per minute. Valid range: 1–80.

input_schema.name: oxygen_saturation
input_schema.description: Peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) as a percentage (e.g., 95.0 for 95%). Valid range: 50–100.

input_schema.name: supplemental_oxygen
input_schema.description: Whether patient is currently receiving any supplemental oxygen. 0 = No, 1 = Yes.

input_schema.name: temperature
input_schema.description: Body temperature in degrees Celsius. Valid range: 25.0–45.0°C.

input_schema.name: systolic_bp
input_schema.description: Systolic blood pressure in mmHg. Valid range: 40–300.

input_schema.name: heart_rate
input_schema.description: Heart rate in beats per minute. Valid range: 10–300.

input_schema.name: avpu_score
input_schema.description: Level of consciousness per AVPU scale.
input_schema.options: "A" = Alert (0 pts), "V" = Responds to Voice (+3 pts), "P" = Responds to Pain (+3 pts), "U" = Unresponsive (+3 pts), "VPU" = Any of V, P, or U (+3 pts)

name: Modified Early Warning Score (MEWS) for Clinical Deterioration
description: The Modified Early Warning Score (MEWS) etermines the degree of illness of a patient using 4 physiological findings and one observation.

input_schema.name: systolic_bp
input_schema.description: Systolic blood pressure in mmHg. Valid range: 1–300 mmHg.

input_schema.name: heart_rate
input_schema.description: Heart rate in beats per minute (bpm). Valid range: 1–300 bpm.

input_schema.name: respiratory_rate
input_schema.description: Respiratory rate in breaths per minute. Valid range: 1–60.

input_schema.name: temperature
input_schema.description: Body temperature in degrees Celsius (°C). Valid range: 25.0–45.0 °C.

input_schema.name: avpu_score
input_schema.description: Level of consciousness on the AVPU scale. Allowed values (case-insensitive): 'Alert' (0 pts), 'Voice' (+1 pt), 'Pain' (+2 pts), 'Unresponsive' (+3 pts). Aliases accepted: 'Reacts to voice' → 'Voice'; 'Reacts to pain' → 'Pain'.

name: Modified Rankin Scale for Neurologic Disability
description: The Modified Rankin Scale (mRS) measures degree of disability/dependence after a stroke.

input_schema.name: baseline_activity
input_schema.description: Patient's baseline activity level.
input_schema.options: 0 - No symptoms at all, 1 - No significant disability despite symptoms; able to carry out all usual duties and activities, 2 - Slight disability; unable to carry out all previous activities, but able to look after own affairs without assistance, 3 - Moderate disability; requiring some help, but able to walk without assistance, 4 - Moderately severe disability; unable to walk and attend to bodily needs without assistance, 5 - Severe disability; bedridden, incontinent and requiring constant nursing care and attention, 6 - Dead

name: DRAGON Score for Post-TPA Stroke Outcome
description: The DRAGON Score for Post-TPA Stroke Outcome predicts 3 month outcome in ischemic stroke patients receiving TPA.

input_schema.name: cerebral_artery
input_schema.description: HyperDense cerebral artery or early infarct on CT.
input_schema.options: No (0 pts), Either (+1 pt), Both (+2 pts)

input_schema.name: mrs_prestroke
input_schema.description: Modified Rankin Scale >1 at pre-stroke baseline.

input_schema.name: age
input_schema.description: Patient age category.

input_schema.name: glucose
input_schema.description: Glucose at baseline >144 mg/dL (8 mmol/L).

input_schema.name: treatment_onset
input_schema.description: Onset of treatment >90 minutes from symptom onset.

input_schema.name: baseline_nihss
input_schema.description: Baseline NIH Stroke Scale score category.

name: Barnes Jewish Hospital Stroke Dysphagia Screen
description: The Barnes Jewish Hospital Stroke Dysphagia Screen assesses ability to swallow without aspiration after stroke.

input_schema.name: glasgow_coma_scale_13
input_schema.description: GCS < 13 at time of assessment.

input_schema.name: facial
input_schema.description: Facial asymmetry or weakness present on exam.

input_schema.name: tongue
input_schema.description: Tongue asymmetry or weakness present on exam.

input_schema.name: palatal
input_schema.description: Palatal asymmetry or weakness present on exam.

input_schema.name: aspiration_signs
input_schema.description: Any signs of aspiration (throat clearing, cough, or voice change) during or within 1 minute after the 3 oz sequential water swallow test. Only evaluated when ALL four screening questions above are answered "No".
input_schema.options: "Yes", "No", or "Not performed" (default when water test was not reached)

name: tPA Contraindications for Ischemic Stroke
description: tPA Contraindications provide inclusion/exclusion criteria when deciding to use tPA on a patient with acute ischemic stroke.

input_schema.name: age_18
input_schema.description: Patient is age ≥18 years.

input_schema.name: diagnosis
input_schema.description: Clinical diagnosis of ischemic stroke causing measurable neurological deficit.

input_schema.name: symptom_onset
input_schema.description: Time of symptom onset (or time last known well) is <4.5 hours.

input_schema.name: hemorrhage
input_schema.description: Intracranial hemorrhage present on non-contrast CT head. [Absolute contraindication]

input_schema.name: sub_hemorrhage
input_schema.description: Clinical presentation suggests subarachnoid hemorrhage (even if CT is negative). [Absolute contraindication]

input_schema.name: surg_trauma_stroke
input_schema.description: Neurosurgery, serious head trauma, or prior stroke within the past 3 months. [Absolute contraindication]

input_schema.name: hypertension
input_schema.description: Uncontrolled hypertension at time of treatment (SBP >185 mmHg or DBP >110 mmHg). [Absolute contraindication; may resolve with parenteral antihypertensives]

input_schema.name: hist_hemorr
input_schema.description: History of prior intracranial hemorrhage. [Absolute contraindication]

input_schema.name: malformation
input_schema.description: Known intracranial arteriovenous malformation, neoplasm, or aneurysm. [Absolute contraindication]

input_schema.name: bleeding
input_schema.description: Active internal bleeding (excluding menses). [Absolute contraindication]

input_schema.name: endocarditis
input_schema.description: Suspected or confirmed infective endocarditis. [Absolute contraindication]

input_schema.name: diathesis
input_schema.description: Known bleeding diathesis (e.g., platelet count <100,000/mm³, heparin use within 48 h with elevated aPTT, current anticoagulant use with INR >1.7 or PT >15 s). [Absolute contraindication]

input_schema.name: glucose
input_schema.description: Blood glucose abnormality (<50 mg/dL [2.8 mmol/L] or >400 mg/dL [22.2 mmol/L]) that fully explains deficits. [Absolute contraindication]

input_schema.name: neoplasm
input_schema.description: Intra-axial intracranial neoplasm. [Absolute contraindication]

input_schema.name: gi_malignancy
input_schema.description: Gastrointestinal malignancy. [Relative contraindication]

input_schema.name: intra_surgery
input_schema.description: Intracranial or intraspinal surgery within the last 3 months. [Absolute contraindication]

input_schema.name: ct
input_schema.description: CT brain imaging shows extensive regions of clear hypoattenuation involving >1/3 of the MCA territory. [Absolute contraindication]

input_schema.name: arch
input_schema.description: Stroke is known or suspected to be associated with aortic arch dissection. [Absolute contraindication]

input_schema.name: minor_stroke
input_schema.description: Stroke symptoms are minor or rapidly improving. [Relative contraindication]

input_schema.name: surgery
input_schema.description: Major surgery within the last 14 days. [Relative contraindication]

input_schema.name: gastro
input_schema.description: Recent gastrointestinal or urinary tract hemorrhage (within 21 days). [Relative contraindication]

input_schema.name: seizure
input_schema.description: Seizure at stroke onset (if residual deficits are postictal). [Relative contraindication]

input_schema.name: art_puncture
input_schema.description: Arterial puncture at a non-compressible site within the last 7 days. [Relative contraindication]

input_schema.name: lumb_puncture
input_schema.description: Lumbar puncture within the last 7 days. [Relative contraindication]

input_schema.name: pericarditis
input_schema.description: Acute pericarditis. [Relative contraindication]

input_schema.name: pregnancy
input_schema.description: Pregnancy or first week postpartum. [Relative contraindication]

input_schema.name: age_80
input_schema.description: Age >80 years. [Relative contraindication]

input_schema.name: stroke
input_schema.description: History of both diabetes and prior ischemic stroke. [Relative contraindication]

input_schema.name: anticoagulant
input_schema.description: Current use of oral anticoagulants regardless of INR. [Relative contraindication]

input_schema.name: nihss_25
input_schema.description: NIHSS score >25. [Relative contraindication]

input_schema.name: multi_infarction
input_schema.description: Imaging evidence of multiple infarctions (lacunar or embolic). [Relative contraindication]

name: Pediatric SIRS, Sepsis, and Septic Shock Criteria
description: The Pediatric SIRS, Sepsis, and Septic Shock Criteria defines the severity of sepsis and septic shock for pediatric patients.

input_schema.name: tachycardia
input_schema.description: Tachycardia or bradycardia (if <1 year).

input_schema.name: tachypnea
input_schema.description: Tachypnea or mechanical ventilation related to an acute process.

input_schema.name: leukocyte
input_schema.description: Abnormal leukocyte count or >10% bands.

input_schema.name: infection
input_schema.description: Suspected or present source of infection.

input_schema.name: severe_sepsis
input_schema.description: Cardiovascular dysfunction OR ARDS OR ≥2 other organ dysfunction criteria met.

input_schema.name: septic_shock
input_schema.description: Cardiovascular dysfunction despite adequate fluid resuscitation.

name: COWS Score for Opiate Withdrawal
description: The COWS Score for Opiate Withdrawal quantifies severity of opiate withdrawal.

input_schema.name: pulse
input_schema.description: Resting Pulse Rate score after patient sits/lies 1 min.

input_schema.name: sweat
input_schema.description: Sweating score (not accounted for by room temp/activity in last 30 minutes).
input_schema.options: 0: No report of chills or flushing, 1: Subjective report of chills or flushing, 2: Flushed or observable moistness on face, 3: Beads of sweat on brow or face, 4: Sweat streaming off face

input_schema.name: restless
input_schema.description: Restlessness observation during assessment.
input_schema.options: 0: Able to sit still, 1: Reports difficulty sitting still, but is able to do so, 3: Frequent shifting or extraneous movements of legs/arms, 5: Unable to sit still for more than a few seconds

input_schema.name: pupil
input_schema.description: Pupil size score.
input_schema.options: 0: Pupils pinned or normal size for room light, 1: Pupils possibly larger than normal for room light, 2: Pupils moderately dilated, 5: Pupils so dilated that only the rim of the iris is visible

input_schema.name: bone
input_schema.description: Bone or joint aches score (only additional component attributed to opiate withdrawal if prior pain exists).
input_schema.options: 0: Not present, 1: Mild diffuse discomfort, 2: Patient reports severe diffuse aching of joints/muscles, 4: Patient is rubbing joints/muscles and unable to sit still

input_schema.name: noise
input_schema.description: Runny nose or tearing score.
input_schema.options: 0: Not present, 1: Nasal stuffiness or unusually moist eyes, 2: Nose running or tearing, 4: Nose constantly running or tears streaming down cheeks

input_schema.name: gi
input_schema.description: GI Upset score.
input_schema.options: 0: No GI symptoms, 1: Stomach cramps, 2: Nausea or loose stool, 3: Vomiting or diarrhea, 5: Multiple episodes of vomiting or diarrhea

input_schema.name: tremor
input_schema.description: Tremor observation of outstretched hands.
input_schema.options: 0: No tremor, 1: Tremor can be felt, but not observed, 2: Slight tremor observable, 4: Gross tremor or muscle twitching

input_schema.name: yawn
input_schema.description: Yawning observation during assessment.
input_schema.options: 0: No yawning, 1: Yawning once or twice during assessment, 2: Yawning three or more times during assessment, 4: Yawning several times/minute

input_schema.name: anxiety
input_schema.description: Anxiety or irritability score.
input_schema.options: 0: None, 1: Patient reports increasing irritability or anxiousness, 2: Patient obviously irritable/anxious, 4: Patient so irritable/anxious that assessment is difficult

input_schema.name: skin
input_schema.description: Gooseflesh skin score.
input_schema.options: 0: Skin is smooth, 3: Piloerection of skin can be felt or hairs standing up on arms, 5: Prominent piloerection

name: DASH Prediction Score for Recurrent VTE
description: The DASH Prediction Score for Recurrent VTE Predicts VTE recurrence: continue vs discontinue anticoagulation at 3-6 months.

input_schema.name: ddimer
input_schema.description: D-dimer abnormal (measured ~1 month after stopping anticoagulation). 0 = No (normal D-dimer), 1 = Yes (abnormal D-dimer).

input_schema.name: age_50
input_schema.description: Patient age ≤50 years. 0 = No (age > 50), 1 = Yes (age ≤ 50).

input_schema.name: male
input_schema.description: Patient is male. 0 = No (female), 1 = Yes (male).

input_schema.name: hormone
input_schema.description: Hormone use at time of initial VTE onset (applicable to females only; if male, must be 0). 0 = No (not on hormones or male patient), 1 = Yes (on hormones at VTE onset).

name: AUDIT-C for Alcohol Use
description: AUDIT-C for Alcohol Use screens for unhealthy alcohol use in patients who may not be alcohol-dependent.

input_schema.name: often
input_schema.description: How often the patient had a drink containing alcohol in the past year.
input_schema.options: Never, Monthly or less, Two to four times a month, Two to three times per week, Four or more times a week

input_schema.name: count
input_schema.description: How many drinks the patient had on a typical drinking day in the past year.
input_schema.options: 1 or 2 drinks, 3 or 4, 5 or 6, 7 to 9, 10 or more

input_schema.name: more
input_schema.description: How often the patient had six or more drinks on one occasion in the past year.
input_schema.options: Never, Less than monthly, Monthly, Weekly, Daily or almost daily

name: POMPE-C Tool for Pulmonary Embolism Mortality
description: The POMPE-C tool predicts mortality for patients with pulmonary embolism with cancer.

input_schema.name: dnr
input_schema.description: Do not resuscitate status. New or existing desire of patient to not be resuscitated from death (verbal or written).

input_schema.name: resp_dist
input_schema.description: Respiratory distress. Obvious anxiety from dyspnea or increased work of breathing.

input_schema.name: uls
input_schema.description: Unilateral leg swelling. Leg or arm with new, noticeable swelling causing asymmetry.

input_schema.name: ams
input_schema.description: Altered mental status. New or different from baseline.

input_schema.name: hr
input_schema.description: Heart rate ≥100 bpm recorded at any point in the past 6 hours.

input_schema.name: rr
input_schema.description: Highest respiratory rate recorded in the past 6 hours, in breaths/min.

input_schema.name: wt
input_schema.description: Patient weight in kg. Internally converted to lbs for the formula (1 kg = 2.20462 lbs).

input_schema.name: sat
input_schema.description: Oxygen saturation on room air in %.

name: Padua Prediction Score for Risk of VTE
description: The Padua Prediction Score is a risk assessment model (RAM) for the identification of patients at risk of VTE.

input_schema.name: ca
input_schema.description: Active cancer. 0 = No, 1 = Yes (+3 pts).

input_schema.name: pvte
input_schema.description: Previous VTE (excluding superficial vein thrombosis). 0 = No, 1 = Yes (+3 pts).

input_schema.name: mobile
input_schema.description: Reduced mobility (bed rest ≥3 days due to patient limitations or physician order). 0 = No, 1 = Yes (+3 pts).

input_schema.name: thromcon
input_schema.description: Already known thrombophilic condition (e.g., defects of antithrombin, protein C or S, factor V Leiden, G20210A prothrombin mutation, antiphospholipid syndrome). 0 = No, 1 = Yes (+3 pts).

input_schema.name: ts
input_schema.description: Recent (≤1 month) trauma and/or surgery. 0 = No, 1 = Yes (+2 pts).

input_schema.name: age
input_schema.description: Elderly age (≥70 years). 0 = No, 1 = Yes (+1 pt).

input_schema.name: hf
input_schema.description: Heart and/or respiratory failure. 0 = No, 1 = Yes (+1 pt).

input_schema.name: miis
input_schema.description: Acute MI and/or ischemic stroke. 0 = No, 1 = Yes (+1 pt).

input_schema.name: inf
input_schema.description: Acute infection and/or rheumatologic disorder. 0 = No, 1 = Yes (+1 pt).

input_schema.name: bmi
input_schema.description: Obesity (BMI ≥30). 0 = No, 1 = Yes (+1 pt).

input_schema.name: hormones
input_schema.description: Ongoing hormonal treatment. 0 = No, 1 = Yes (+1 pt).

name: Lille Model for Alcoholic Hepatitis
description: The Lille Model for Alcoholic Hepatitis predicts mortality in patients with Alcoholic Hepatitis not responding to steroid therapy.

input_schema.name: age
input_schema.description: Patient age in years.

input_schema.name: alb
input_schema.description: Serum albumin at admission (day 0) in g/L.
input_schema.options: Valid range: 10–60 g/L (1–6 g/dL). Convert g/dL × 10 = g/L.

input_schema.name: bili_init
input_schema.description: Serum bilirubin at admission (day 0) in µmol/L.
input_schema.options: Valid range: 0–342.08 µmol/L (0–20 mg/dL). Convert mg/dL × 17.104 = µmol/L.

input_schema.name: bili7
input_schema.description: Serum bilirubin at day 7 of steroid therapy in µmol/L.
input_schema.options: Valid range: 0–342.08 µmol/L (0–20 mg/dL). Convert mg/dL × 17.104 = µmol/L.

input_schema.name: cr
input_schema.description: Serum creatinine at admission in µmol/L.
input_schema.options: Valid range: 0–884 µmol/L (0–10 mg/dL). Convert mg/dL × 88.4 = µmol/L. Threshold for renal insufficiency: >115 µmol/L (>1.3 mg/dL).

input_schema.name: pt
input_schema.description: Prothrombin time at admission in seconds.

name: HAT (Hemorrhage After Thrombolysis) Score for Predicting Post-tPA Hemorrhage
description: The HAT (Hemorrhage After thrombolysis) Score assesses hemorrhage risk after tPA.

input_schema.name: hist
input_schema.description: History of diabetes mellitus OR initial serum glucose >200 mg/dL.

input_schema.name: nihss_score
input_schema.description: Pre-tPA NIH Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score category.

input_schema.name: hypodensity
input_schema.description: Easily visible hypodensity on initial non-contrast head CT.
input_schema.options: "No" → 0 points (no visible hypodensity), "<1/3" → 1 point (hypodensity involving < 1/3 of MCA territory), "≥1/3" → 2 points (hypodensity involving ≥ 1/3 of MCA territory)

name: ABC/2 Formula for Intracerebral Hemorrhage Volume
description: The ABC/2 Formula for Intracerebral Hemorrhage Volume predicts size of intracranial hemorrhage.

input_schema.name: hemm_shape
input_schema.description: Hemorrhage morphology on CT. Must be one of: 'Round or Ellipsoid' (smooth, round, or ovoid hematoma → divisor = 2) or 'Irregular, Separated, or Multinodular' (irregular margins, satellite collections, or multilobular shape → divisor = 3).
input_schema.options: Round or Ellipsoid, Irregular, Separated, or Multinodular

input_schema.name: bl_length
input_schema.description: Length (A) — longest diameter of hemorrhage on the CT slice with the largest area of hemorrhage. Unit: cm. Valid range: 0.1–100 cm.

input_schema.name: bl_width
input_schema.description: Width (B) — diameter perpendicular to the length on the same CT slice with the largest area of hemorrhage. Unit: cm. Valid range: 0.1–100 cm.

input_schema.name: slices
input_schema.description: Number of CT slices on which hemorrhage is present. Counting rule — slice with ≥75% hemorrhage area counts as 1; 25–75% area counts as 0.5; <25% area counts as 0. Unit: slices. Valid range: 0.1–10.

input_schema.name: sl_thick
input_schema.description: CT slice thickness. Unit: mm. Valid range: 0.1–1000 mm. NOTE: CT slice thickness is typically entered in mm, not cm.

name: SEDAN Score for Post-tPA Hemorrhage
description: The SEDAN score assesses symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH) risk after thrombolysis.

input_schema.name: gluc
input_schema.description: Blood sugar category at time of treatment: 0 = <145 mg/dL (<8.1 mmol/L) → 0 pts, 1 = 145–216 mg/dL (8.1–12.0 mmol/L) → 1 pt, 2 = >216 mg/dL (>12.0 mmol/L) → 2 pts

input_schema.name: infarct
input_schema.description: Early infarct signs on initial CT: 0 = No → 0 pts, 1 = Yes → 1 pt

input_schema.name: ct
input_schema.description: Hyperdense cerebral artery sign on initial CT: 0 = No → 0 pts, 1 = Yes → 1 pt

input_schema.name: age
input_schema.description: Patient age > 75 years: 0 = No (age ≤ 75) → 0 pts, 1 = Yes (age > 75) → 1 pt

input_schema.name: nihss
input_schema.description: NIH Stroke Scale score ≥ 10 at presentation: 0 = No (NIHSS < 10) → 0 pts, 1 = Yes (NIHSS ≥ 10) → 1 pt

name: Steroid Conversion Calculator
description: The Steroid Conversion Calculator converts steroid dosages using dosing equivalencies.

input_schema.name: drug_input
input_schema.description: The steroid being converted FROM.
input_schema.options: "Betamethasone (IV)", "Cortisone (PO)", "Dexamethasone (IV or PO)", "Hydrocortisone (IV or PO)", "MethylPrednisoLONE (IV or PO)", "PrednisoLONE (PO)", "PredniSONE (PO)", "Triamcinolone (IV)"

input_schema.name: drug_dosage
input_schema.description: Dose of the input steroid in mg. Valid range: 0–1000 mg.

input_schema.name: drug_output
input_schema.description: The steroid being converted TO.
input_schema.options: "Betamethasone (IV)", "Cortisone (PO)", "Dexamethasone (IV or PO)", "Hydrocortisone (IV or PO)", "MethylPrednisoLONE (IV or PO)", "PrednisoLONE (IV or PO)", "PredniSONE (PO)", "Triamcinolone (IV)"

name: STONE Nephrolithometry Score for Renal Calculi
description: The STONE Nephrolithotomy Scoring System predicts severity of kidney stone based radiological visualization.

input_schema.name: size
input_schema.description: Stone size in mm² (length × width measured on CT).

input_schema.name: tract
input_schema.description: Tract length in mm (distance from stone center to skin measured on CT at 0°, 45°, and 90°).

input_schema.name: obstruction
input_schema.description: Degree of hydronephrosis on imaging.

input_schema.name: calyces
input_schema.description: Number of calyces involved by calculi.

input_schema.name: essence
input_schema.description: Stone density (essence) measured in Hounsfield units (HU) on non-contrast CT.

name: Urine Anion Gap
description: The Urine Anion Gap is used for differential diagnosis in metabolic acidosis using measured ions in the urine.

input_schema.name: na
input_schema.description: Urine sodium concentration in mmol/L (equivalent to mEq/L).

input_schema.name: k
input_schema.description: Urine potassium concentration in mmol/L (equivalent to mEq/L).

input_schema.name: cl
input_schema.description: Urine chloride concentration in mmol/L (equivalent to mEq/L).

name: UCSF-CAPRA Score for Prostate Cancer Risk
description: The UCSF-CAPRA (Cancer of the Prostate Risk Assessment) Score predicts outcomes of patients post-treatment for prostate cancer.

input_schema.name: age
input_schema.description: Patient age category at diagnosis: 0 = < 50 years (0 pts), 1 = >= 50 years (+1 pt)

input_schema.name: psa
input_schema.description: PSA at diagnosis category (ng/mL): 0 = < 6 ng/mL (0 pts), 1 = >= 6 to 10 ng/mL (+1 pt), 2 = >= 10 to 20 ng/mL (+2 pts), 3 = >= 20 to 30 ng/mL (+3 pts), 4 = > 30 ng/mL (+4 pts)

input_schema.name: gleason
input_schema.description: Gleason Score pattern — primary or secondary: 0 = No 4 or 5 pattern present (0 pts), 1 = 4 or 5 pattern in secondary (+1 pt), 3 = 4 or 5 pattern in primary (+3 pts)

input_schema.name: stage
input_schema.description: Clinical stage: 0 = T1 or T2 (0 pts), 1 = T3a (+1 pt)

input_schema.name: biopsy
input_schema.description: Percent biopsy cores positive for cancer: 0 = < 34% (0 pts), 1 = >= 34% (+1 pt)

name: Revised Urinary Incontinence Scale (RUIS)
description: The Revised Urinary Incontinence Scale (RUIS) assess urinary incontinence and monitors patient outcomes following treatment.

input_schema.name: urgency
input_schema.description: Urine leakage related to the feeling of urgency.

input_schema.name: activity
input_schema.description: Urine leakage related to physical activity, coughing, or sneezing.

input_schema.name: drops
input_schema.description: Small amounts of urine leakage (drops).

input_schema.name: leakfreq
input_schema.description: How often the patient experiences urine leakage.
input_schema.options: "Never" (0), "Less than once a month" (1), "A few times a month" (2), "A few times a week" (3), "Every day and/or night" (4)

input_schema.name: lose
input_schema.description: How much urine is lost each time.

name: Gleason Score for Prostate Cancer
description: The Gleason Score for Prostate Cancer provides prognosis based on microscopic tumor appearance.

input_schema.name: primary
input_schema.description: Primary grade — dominant pattern representing >50% of total pattern seen. Valid values: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

input_schema.name: secondary
input_schema.description: Secondary grade — highest-grade pattern seen after the primary pattern. Valid values: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

input_schema.name: tertiary
input_schema.description: Tertiary grade — third pattern present in the biopsy, if identifiable. Valid values: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

name: D'Amico Risk Classification for Prostate Cancer
description: The D'Amico Risk Classification for Prostate Cancer assesses 5 year failure of treatment based on clinical factors.

input_schema.name: psa
input_schema.description: PSA level category (ng/mL).

input_schema.name: gleason
input_schema.description: Gleason score category.

input_schema.name: stage
input_schema.description: Clinical tumor stage category.

name: Urine Output and Fluid Balance
description: The Urine Output and Fluid Balance calculates urine output over a 24 hour period and fluid balance based on urine output (assuming no other fluid losses).

input_schema.name: wt
input_schema.description: Patient weight in kg. Valid range: 0.5–226.8 kg (supports neonates through adults).

input_schema.name: uop
input_schema.description: Total urine output in mL over the measurement period. Valid range: 1–5000 mL.

input_schema.name: hrs
input_schema.description: Duration of the urine collection period in hours. Valid range: 0.999–24.001 h.

input_schema.name: ins
input_schema.description: Fluid intake in mL over the same measurement period (optional). Valid range: 1–5000 mL. When provided, a net fluid-balance estimate is calculated. Pass None (default) to omit.

name: NEXUS Chest Decision Instrument for Blunt Chest Trauma
description: The NEXUS Chest Decision Instrument for Blunt Chest Trauma aids in the decision making process for imaging patients with blunt chest trauma.

input_schema.name: age
input_schema.description: Patient age >60 years. 0 = No, 1 = Yes.

input_schema.name: mech
input_schema.description: Rapid deceleration mechanism (fall >6 m or MVC >64 km/h). 0 = No, 1 = Yes.

input_schema.name: cp
input_schema.description: Chest pain present. 0 = No, 1 = Yes.

input_schema.name: intox
input_schema.description: Intoxication (alcohol, drugs, or clinical signs of intoxication). 0 = No, 1 = Yes.

input_schema.name: ams
input_schema.description: Altered mental status. 0 = No, 1 = Yes.

input_schema.name: injury
input_schema.description: Distracting painful injury (any condition thought to produce sufficient pain to distract from a second intrathoracic injury, e.g. long bone fractures, large lacerations, major burns). 0 = No, 1 = Yes.

input_schema.name: ttp
input_schema.description: Tenderness to chest wall palpation. Note: clavicular tenderness does NOT qualify. 0 = No, 1 = Yes.

name: Prostate Tumor Volume & Density
description: The Prostate Tumor Volume & Density calculator measures prostate tumor volume and PSA density.

input_schema.name: pro_length
input_schema.description: Prostate length in cm. Valid range: 0.1–100 cm.

input_schema.name: pro_width
input_schema.description: Prostate width in cm. Valid range: 0.1–100 cm.

input_schema.name: pro_height
input_schema.description: Prostate height in cm. Valid range: 0.1–100 cm.

input_schema.name: psa
input_schema.description: Serum PSA (prostate-specific antigen) value in ng/mL. Valid range: 0–100 ng/mL.

name: Kruis Score for Diagnosis of Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS)
description: The Kruis Score for Diagnosis of Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) determines presence of IBS using clinically significant weighted criteria.

input_schema.name: pfi
input_schema.description: Symptoms of abdominal pain, flatulence, or bowel irregularity.

input_schema.name: duration
input_schema.description: Symptom duration > 2 years.

input_schema.name: abdpain
input_schema.description: Pain described as burning, cutting, very strong, terrible, feeling of pressure, dull, boring, or 'not so bad'.

input_schema.name: dc
input_schema.description: Alternating constipation and diarrhea.

input_schema.name: abnl
input_schema.description: Abnormal physical findings or history pathognomonic of another disease (red flag).

input_schema.name: esr
input_schema.description: ESR > 10 mm/hr (red flag).

input_schema.name: wbc
input_schema.description: WBC > 10,000/µL (red flag).

input_schema.name: anemia
input_schema.description: Anemia (hemoglobin < 12 g/dL in females, < 14 g/dL in males) (red flag).

input_schema.name: blood
input_schema.description: History of blood in stool (red flag).

name: Manchester Score for Prognosis in Small Cell Lung Cancer
description: The Manchester Score for Prognosis in Small Cell Lung Cancer predicts 2 year survival of small cell lung cancer.

input_schema.name: ldh
input_schema.description: Serum LDH > upper limit of normal.

input_schema.name: na
input_schema.description: Serum sodium < 132 mmol/L.

input_schema.name: alk_phos
input_schema.description: Serum alkaline phosphatase > 1.5x the upper limit of normal.

input_schema.name: bicarb
input_schema.description: Serum bicarbonate < 24 mmol/L.

input_schema.name: stage
input_schema.description: Extensive stage disease.

input_schema.name: karnofsky
input_schema.description: Karnofsky Performance Status score.

name: Sokal Index for Chronic Myelogenous Leukemia (CML)
description: The Sokal Index for CML predicts survival of CML based on clinical and lab information.

input_schema.name: age
input_schema.description: Patient age in years. Valid range: 0.1–100 years.

input_schema.name: spl
input_schema.description: Spleen size in cm — maximum distance palpable below the costal margin on physical examination. Valid range: 0–10 cm.

input_schema.name: plt
input_schema.description: Platelet count in × 10⁹/L (equivalent to × 10³/µL). Valid range: 10–750 × 10⁹/L.

input_schema.name: blasts
input_schema.description: Percentage of myeloblasts in peripheral blood (%). Valid range: 0–100 %.

name: Critical Care Pain Observation Tool (CPOT)
description: The Critical Care Pain Observation Tool (CPOT) rates critically ill patients’ pain based on clinical observation.

input_schema.name: intubated
input_schema.description: Whether the patient is intubated; determines which sub-scale (vent vs vocal) is used.

input_schema.name: vent
input_schema.description: Compliance with ventilator — used ONLY when intubated == "Yes".

input_schema.name: lesions
input_schema.description: "Yes" if objective clinical evidence of ≥2 lesions on MRI, "No" otherwise.

input_schema.name: none

input_schema.name: perivent
input_schema.description: "Yes" if ≥1 periventricular T2 lesion present on MRI, "No" otherwise.

input_schema.name: juxta

input_schema.name: infra
input_schema.description: "Yes" if ≥1 infratentorial T2 lesion present on MRI, "No" otherwise.

input_schema.name: spine

input_schema.name: simultaneous
input_schema.description: "Yes" if simultaneous presence of asymptomatic gadolinium-enhancing and non-enhancing lesions at any time, "No" otherwise.

input_schema.name: prog
input_schema.description: "Yes" if ≥1 year of disease progression (prospective or retrospective), "No" otherwise. Required for PPMS pathway.

input_schema.name: disspine
input_schema.description: "Yes" if evidence of dissemination in space in the spinal cord (≥2 T2 bright lesions in spinal cord, for PPMS criterion), "No" otherwise.

input_schema.name: csf

input_schema.name: int1

input_schema.name: int2

input_schema.name: int3
input_schema.description: Dissociative reactions, e.g. flashbacks, where individual feels or acts as if the traumatic event were recurring; may occur on a continuum, with the most extreme expression being complete loss of awareness of present surroundings; in children, trauma-specific reenactment may occur in play.

input_schema.name: int4
input_schema.description: Intense or prolonged psychological distress at exposure to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.

input_schema.name: int5
input_schema.description: Marked physiological reactions to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.

input_schema.name: av1

input_schema.name: av2

name: ARISCAT Score for Postoperative Pulmonary Complications
description: The ARISCAT score is a tool used to assess the risk of postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) in patients undergoing surgery. It evaluates seven preoperative factors, including age, preoperative oxygen saturation, respiratory infection in the last month, anemia, and type of surgery, to predict the likelihood of PPCs. This scoring system helps healthcare providers identify high-risk patients, enabling targeted preventive measures to reduce complications.
input_schema:
Calculate the ARISCAT Score for Postoperative Pulmonary Complications.
    This score helps predict the risk of pulmonary complications in patients undergoing surgery under general, neuraxial, or regional anesthesia.

    Parameters:
    age (int): Patient's age in years.
    spo2 (int): Preoperative oxygen saturation (SpO2) percentage.
    respiratory_infection (int): Indicates the presence of respiratory infection in the last month. 0 for 'No', 1 for 'Yes'.
    anemia (int): Indicates preoperative anemia (Hgb ≤10 g/dL). 0 for 'No', 1 for 'Yes'.
    surgical_incision (int): Type of surgical incision. 0 for 'Peripheral', 1 for 'Upper abdominal', 2 for 'Intrathoracic'.
    surgery_duration (int): Duration of the surgery in hours.
    emergency (int): Indicates if the procedure was an emergency. 0 for 'No', 1 for 'Yes'.

    Returns:
    int: The ARISCAT score, which is a summation of points based on the provided parameters.

name: Morphine Milligram Equivalents (MME) Calculator
description: The Morphine Milligram Equivalents (MME) Calculator is used to convert various opioid dosages into a standardized morphine equivalent to help assess opioid use risk and ensure safe dosing. It is particularly useful in clinical settings where healthcare providers manage patients with chronic pain or are prescribing multiple opioids. The tool aids in maintaining dosage safety and compliance with guidelines to minimize the risk of opioid misuse and overdose.
input_schema:
Calculate the Morphine Milligram Equivalents (MME) per day based on the opioid dosage,
    number of doses per day, and the drug used. This function can handle multiple drugs
    to compute total MME/day by summing up MME for each drug.

    Parameters:
    - dosages (list of float): List of dosages for each drug in the units appropriate for the drug
      (mcg/hr for fentanyl patches, mcg for fentanyl buccal/sublingual tablets, and mg for all other opioids).
    - doses_per_day (list of int): List of doses per day for each corresponding drug.
    - drugs (list of int): List of indexes representing drugs where each index corresponds to:
      0: Codeine, 1: Fentanyl buccal or sublingual, 2: Fentanyl patch, 3: Hydrocodone,
      4: Hydromorphone, 5: Methadone, 6: Morphine, 7: Oxycodone, 8: Oxymorphone,
      9: Tapentadol, 10: Tramadol, 11: Buprenorphine (excluded from calculation).

    Returns:
    - float: Total MME/day calculated across all provided drugs.

    Note:
    - The conversion factors are based on standard estimates and may not account for individual differences.
    - Buprenorphine is not included in the calculations as per its unique pharmacological profile.

name: Centor Score (Modified/McIsaac) for Strep Pharyngitis
description: The Centor Score, also known as the Modified Centor Score or McIsaac Score, is a clinical tool used to assess the likelihood of streptococcal pharyngitis in patients presenting with a sore throat. It evaluates factors such as age, fever, tonsillar exudates, tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy, and absence of cough to guide clinicians on whether to perform further testing or prescribe antibiotics. This scoring system helps reduce unnecessary antibiotic use by identifying patients who are most likely to benefit from streptococcal testing.
input_schema:
Calculate the Centor Score (Modified/McIsaac) for Strep Pharyngitis.
    
    This scoring system helps clinicians determine the likelihood of Group A Streptococcus (GAS) 
    in patients with symptoms of pharyngitis, which is critical for deciding whether to proceed 
    with testing for strep pharyngitis. The score integrates factors such as age, tonsillar exudate, 
    cervical lymphadenopathy, temperature, and the presence of cough to stratify the risk.
    
    Parameters:
    - age (int): Age of the patient in years.
    - exudate_swelling (bool): True if there is exudate or swelling on the tonsils, False otherwise.
    - tender_swollen_lymph_nodes (bool): True if there are tender/swollen anterior cervical lymph nodes, False otherwise.
    - temperature (float): Patient's temperature in degrees Celsius.
    - cough (bool): True if cough is present, False otherwise.

    Returns:
    - int: The calculated Centor Score, which ranges from -1 to 4.
    
    Usage:
    Typically used in primary care settings to assess the necessity for further testing for GAS infection,
    guiding the judicious use of antibiotics in managing pharyngitis. Higher scores suggest a higher probability
    of streptococcal infection and may warrant testing and/or treatment.

name: Free Water Deficit in Hypernatremia
description: The Free Water Deficit (FWD) calculation is used in the management of hypernatremia to estimate the amount of water required to normalize a patient's serum sodium concentration. It is particularly useful in clinical settings for patients with elevated sodium levels due to water loss or low water intake. This calculation helps guide appropriate fluid replacement strategies, ensuring both the safety and effectiveness of treatment.
input_schema:
Calculate the Free Water Deficit (FWD) in a patient with hypernatremia.

    The FWD is a measure used in the management of hypernatremia to determine the amount
    of water a patient needs to ingest or be given intravenously to reach normal serum
    sodium levels without inducing cellular edema.

    Parameters:
    - gender_age_group (int): Index representing the patient's gender and age group.
      - 0: Adult male
      - 1: Adult female
      - 2: Elderly male
      - 3: Elderly female
      - 4: Child
    - weight_kg (float): The weight of the patient in kilograms.
    - current_na (float): The current serum sodium level of the patient (mmol/L).
    - ideal_na (float): The target or ideal serum sodium level for the patient (mmol/L).

    Returns:
    - float: The calculated free water deficit in liters.

    Usage:
    Calculate the free water deficit for an elderly female weighing 70 kg with a current
    sodium level of 155 mmol/L and an ideal sodium level of 140 mmol/L:
    >>> calculate_free_water_deficit(3, 70, 155, 140)

name: Wells' Criteria for Pulmonary Embolism
description: Wells' Criteria for Pulmonary Embolism is a clinical tool used to assess the probability of pulmonary embolism (PE) in patients presenting with symptoms suggestive of this condition. It involves scoring various clinical factors and symptoms to categorize the likelihood of PE as low, moderate, or high. This tool guides clinicians in deciding whether further diagnostic testing, such as a D-dimer test or imaging, is necessary.
input_schema:
Calculates the Wells' Criteria for Pulmonary Embolism (PE).
    
    This function estimates the pre-test probability of pulmonary embolism based on certain clinical criteria.
    It helps in stratifying patients into different risk categories which then guides further diagnostic testing like d-dimer or CT angiogram.
    
    Parameters:
    dvt_symptoms (bool): True if there are clinical signs and symptoms of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), else False.
    pe_diagnosis (bool): True if pulmonary embolism is the #1 diagnosis or equally likely, else False.
    heart_rate (bool): True if heart rate is over 100, else False.
    immobilization_surgery (bool): True if patient has been immobilized for at least 3 days or had surgery in the past 4 weeks, else False.
    previous_pe_dvt (bool): True if there is a history of previously diagnosed PE or DVT, else False.
    hemoptysis (bool): True if the patient has hemoptysis, else False.
    malignancy (bool): True if the patient has malignancy with treatment within the last 6 months or is on palliative, else False.
    
    Returns:
    float: The total score based on Wells' Criteria, which can be used to estimate the risk of pulmonary embolism.
    
    Application:
    This score should be used in conjunction with clinical judgment in patients who have a suspicion of pulmonary embolism.
    It is validated for both inpatient and emergency department settings.
    Not suitable for all patients with chest pain or shortness of breath without a clinical suspicion of PE.

name: Anion Gap
description: The Anion Gap is a diagnostic tool used to help identify disturbances in acid-base balance in the body, typically by calculating the difference between primary measured cations and anions in serum. It is particularly useful in clinical settings for diagnosing the causes of metabolic acidosis, such as renal failure, diabetic ketoacidosis, or poisoning. Physicians often use this calculation when a patient presents with altered mental status, unexplained nausea, fatigue, or breathing difficulties.
input_schema:
Calculate the Anion Gap using sodium, chloride, and bicarbonate levels.

    The Anion Gap is a measure used in medicine to help diagnose the presence of an acidosis and whether it has an elevated anion gap. This calculation is essential in identifying the type of acidosis a patient might have, differentiating between gap and non-gap acidoses. Elevated Anion Gap suggests the presence of additional unmeasured anions in the blood, which could indicate conditions like ketoacidosis, lactic acidosis, or poisoning by substances such as methanol.

    Parameters:
    sodium (float): Sodium level in mEq/L.
    chloride (float): Chloride level in mEq/L.
    bicarbonate (float): Bicarbonate level in mEq/L.

    Returns:
    float: The calculated Anion Gap in mEq/L.

    Example:
    >>> calculate_anion_gap(140, 104, 24)
    12.0

name: PHQ-9 (Patient Health Questionnaire-9)
description: The PHQ-9 (Patient Health Questionnaire-9) is a widely used self-administered diagnostic tool for assessing the presence and severity of depression. It consists of nine questions that align with the diagnostic criteria for depression from the DSM-IV (Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders). Clinicians typically use the PHQ-9 in both medical and mental health settings to screen for depression during routine health assessments and to monitor treatment progress.
input_schema:
Calculate the PHQ-9 (Patient Health Questionnaire-9) score.

    The PHQ-9 is a clinical scale used to diagnose depression and to quantify and monitor the severity of depression symptoms.
    It evaluates symptoms based on the 9 DSM criteria for major depressive disorder (MDD). Each criterion is scored from 0 to 3:
    - "0" for 'Not at all'
    - "1" for 'Several days'
    - "2" for 'More than half the days'
    - "3" for 'Nearly every day'
    The function sums these scores to provide an overall severity score ranging from 0 to 27.

    Parameters:
    - interest_pleasure (int): Index from 0 to 3 indicating frequency of little interest or pleasure in doing things.
    - feeling_down (int): Index from 0 to 3 indicating frequency of feeling down, depressed, or hopeless.
    - sleep_issues (int): Index from 0 to 3 indicating trouble with falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much.
    - tired_energy (int): Index from 0 to 3 indicating feeling tired or having little energy.
    - appetite_issues (int): Index from 0 to 3 indicating issues with poor appetite or overeating.
    - self_feeling (int): Index from 0 to 3 indicating feelings of being bad about oneself, or feeling like a failure.
    - concentration (int): Index from 0 to 3 indicating trouble concentrating on things.
    - activity_level (int): Index from 0 to 3 indicating altered activity levels, either moving too slowly or being too fidgety.
    - suicidal_thoughts (int): Index from 0 to 3 indicating frequency of thoughts of self-harm or being better off dead.

    Returns:
    - int: The total PHQ-9 score, which is the sum of all the individual scores for the symptoms listed above.

name: GAD-7 (General Anxiety Disorder-7)
description: The GAD-7 (General Anxiety Disorder-7) is a self-administered questionnaire used to screen for and measure the severity of generalized anxiety disorder. It consists of seven questions that evaluate the frequency of anxiety symptoms over the past two weeks. This tool is widely used in clinical settings and research to facilitate the diagnosis and monitoring of anxiety.
input_schema:
Calculate the GAD-7 (General Anxiety Disorder-7) score. This function computes the total score 
    based on seven items that assess the severity of various signs of anxiety according to their 
    frequency over the past two weeks. Each item is scored from 0 to 3 (0 = Not at all, 1 = Several days,
    2 = More than half the days, 3 = Nearly every day).

    This scale is a quick screening tool for detecting the presence of clinically significant anxiety disorders 
    including Generalized Anxiety Disorder, Panic Disorder, Social Phobia, and Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder.
    It is highly sensitive and specific across various cutoffs, used extensively in primary care and mental health settings 
    to assess and monitor treatment responses.

    Parameters:
    - nervous (int): Score for feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge.
    - control_worrying (int): Score for not being able to stop or control worrying.
    - worry_too_much (int): Score for worrying too much about different things.
    - trouble_relaxing (int): Score for having trouble relaxing.
    - restlessness (int): Score for being so restless that it is hard to sit still.
    - irritability (int): Score for becoming easily annoyed or irritable.
    - fear_of_awful_events (int): Score for feeling afraid as if something awful might happen.

    Returns:
    int: The total GAD-7 score, ranging from 0 to 21.

    Usage Example:
    gad_7_score = calculate_gad_7(3, 2, 1, 3, 0, 2, 1)
    print(f"GAD-7 Score: {gad_7_score}") # Outputs the calculated GAD-7 score

name: CIWA-Ar for Alcohol Withdrawal
description: The Clinical Institute Withdrawal Assessment for Alcohol, Revised (CIWA-Ar) is a tool used to assess the severity of alcohol withdrawal symptoms and guide treatment decisions. It is commonly used in hospital settings, particularly in emergency departments and detoxification units, to monitor withdrawal progression and determine the need for medication. The CIWA-Ar evaluates symptoms such as tremors, agitation, and hallucinations, facilitating targeted and safe management of withdrawal.
input_schema:
Calculate the CIWA-Ar scale score for assessing alcohol withdrawal severity.

    The CIWA-Ar scale is intended for use in various medical settings where alcohol withdrawal is suspected.
    This tool helps in quantifying the severity of alcohol withdrawal through several symptom dimensions,
    each scored independently. The cumulative score helps guide clinical decisions regarding the necessity
    and intensity of treatment for withdrawal.

    Parameters:
    nausea_vomiting (int): Index for nausea and vomiting severity. Range: 0-7.
        - 0: No nausea and no vomiting
        - 1: Mild nausea and no vomiting
        - 2-3: More severe nausea without vomiting
        - 4: Intermittent nausea with dry heaves
        - 5-6: Increasing severity of nausea and dry heaves
        - 7: Constant nausea, frequent dry heaves and vomiting
    tremor (int): Index for tremor severity. Range: 0-7.
        - 0: No tremor
        - 1: Not visible, but can be felt fingertip to fingertip
        - 2-3: More severe tremors without visible shaking
        - 4: Moderate tremor with arms extended
        - 5-6: Severe tremor, visible with arms extended
        - 7: Very severe tremor, even with arms not extended
    paroxysmal_sweats (int): Index for sweating severity. Range: 0-7.
        - 0: No sweat visible
        - 1: Barely perceptible sweating, palms moist
        - 2-3: More perceptible sweating without drenching
        - 4: Beads of sweat obvious on forehead
        - 5-6: Severe sweating
        - 7: Drenching sweats
    anxiety (int): Index for anxiety level. Range: 0-7.
        - 0: No anxiety, at ease
        - 1: Mildly anxious
        - 2-3: Moderate anxiety
        - 4: Moderately anxious, or guarded, so anxiety is inferred
        - 5-6: Severe anxiety, similar to panic states
        - 7: Equivalent to acute panic states as seen in severe delirium or acute schizophrenic reactions
    agitation (int): Index for agitation level. Range: 0-7.
        - 0: Normal activity
        - 1: Somewhat more activity than normal
        - 2-3: More active, moderately fidgety and restless
        - 4: Moderately fidgety and restless
        - 5-6: Severe restlessness
        - 7: Paces back and forth during most of the interview, or constantly thrashes about
    tactile_disturbances (int): Index for tactile disturbances. Range: 0-7.
        - 0: None
        - 1-2: Mild to moderate itching, pin and needles, burning, or numbness
        - 3-4: Moderate to moderately severe hallucinations
        - 5-6: Severe to extremely severe hallucinations
        - 7: Continuous hallucinations
    visual_disturbances (int): Index for visual disturbances. Range: 0-7.
        - 0: No visual disturbances
        - 1-2: Mild to moderate sensitivity
        - 3-4: Moderate to moderately severe hallucinations
        - 5-6: Severe to extremely severe hallucinations
        - 7: Continuous hallucinations
    headache_fullness (int): Index for headache or fullness in head. Range: 0-7.
        - 0: No headache
        - 1-2: Mild to moderate headache
        - 3-4: Moderate to moderately severe headache
        - 5-6: Severe to very severe headache
        - 7: Extremely severe headache
    orientation_sensorium (int): Index for orientation or clouding of sensorium. Range: 0-4.
        - 0: Fully oriented, can do serial additions
        - 1: Can't do serial additions or is uncertain about date
        - 2: Disoriented for date by no more than 2 calendar days
        - 3: Disoriented for date by more than 2 calendar days
        - 4: Disoriented to place or person

    Returns:
    int: The total CIWA-Ar score, representing the severity of alcohol withdrawal.

    Usage:
    score = calculate_ciwa_ar(2, 4, 1, 3, 5, 2, 0, 6, 1)
    print("CIWA-Ar score:", score)

name: Revised Cardiac Risk Index for Pre-Operative Risk
description: The Revised Cardiac Risk Index (RCRI) is a clinical tool used to estimate the risk of major cardiac complications, like heart attacks or cardiac arrest, in patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery. It evaluates risk based on six pre-operative criteria, including history of ischemic heart disease, congestive heart failure, and insulin therapy for diabetes, among others. This index aids healthcare providers in identifying high-risk patients who may benefit from further cardiac evaluation or specific perioperative management strategies.
input_schema:
Calculate the Revised Cardiac Risk Index for Pre-Operative Risk.

    This function calculates the Revised Cardiac Risk Index, which is used to assess the risk of major cardiac complications in patients undergoing elective or urgent/semi-urgent non-cardiac surgery. It is based on a set of specific risk factors and is valuable for risk stratification and aiding discussions about informed consent with patients.

    Parameters:
    elevated_risk_surgery (bool): True if the surgery is intraperitoneal, intrathoracic, or suprainguinal vascular.
    history_of_ischemic_heart_disease (bool): True if there is a history of myocardial infarction, positive exercise test, current chest pain considered due to myocardial ischemia, or use of nitrate therapy or ECG showing pathological Q waves.
    history_of_congestive_heart_failure (bool): True if there are signs such as pulmonary edema, bilateral rales or S3 gallop, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, or chest X-ray showing pulmonary vascular redistribution.
    history_of_cerebrovascular_disease (bool): True if there is a history of transient ischemic attack or stroke.
    preop_treatment_with_insulin (bool): True if the patient is being treated with insulin pre-operatively.
    preop_creatinine_above_threshold (bool): True if pre-operative creatinine levels are greater than 2 mg/dL or 176.8 µmol/L.

    Returns:
